observations: Art: Inspected all 36 final Art images across six labelled sheets. The other five body meshes retain their prior geometry, open cabins and glazing/trim; there is no new missing body panel or opaque centre pane.

Art: Inspected current Urus side and front-quarter PNGs at original resolution and the saved pass9 side view at original resolution. The upper door highlight is steadier, the central sheet broader and the handle recesses less pinched. The intake, bonnet, projector and rear hatch details remain visible across all six directions.

Art: Compared the new surface with the official V8 Urus brochure front-quarter views5/14. This is an incremental side-surface correction; front/rear fascia corners, greenhouse, trim, interiors and broad body curvature remain simplified. The other five bodies were retained, not newly rebuilt.

Detail: Inspected all six current Detail images and the meadow-close PNG at original resolution. Scanned plant clusters are smaller and less overlapped than pass9, and meadow planting mixes small tufts with retained taller procedural blades. The ground palette is more muted/olive while retaining photographic soil and leafy detail.
Detail: Snow grain, shallow wind ripples, drift relief and the broken snow/soil fringe are retained. The snow scene has no new dark floor or visible material seam.

Detail: Remaining limits include sparse large procedural grass blades, repeated ground motifs and blocky acquired snow-cliff silhouettes. This is improved plant scale, not a dense production meadow or a winter landscape rebuild.

Ruts: Inspected all 16 current rut PNGs. Mud and wet-grass channels remain continuous and rounded with darker exposed soil, while firm dirt/sand stay lighter and shallow. Actual Jeep motor-drive paths remain continuous behind the vehicle.

Ruts: Snow floors retain pale blue-grey compaction and white shoulders with visible tread shading. The meadow palette/plant edits do not turn soft-ground tracks into black rubber. Physical soil geometry is retained; these are bounded height-field grooves rather than granular particles.
